title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1971-03-24
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel (7.5ips 1/4 Track) -> Master Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a scorching 1971 Winterland show, highlighted by a smoking The Other One and hard‑rocking Hard to Handle with crystal‑clear, well‑balanced mix.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers pristine soundboard quality – clear, balanced and benefiting from the famed CM upgrades. Musically the night is a barn‑burner: a powerful second set with standout versions of The Other One, Hard to Handle, King Bee and the NFA > GDTRFB > NFA combo, while the first set is viewed as merely adequate. Overall the band sounds locked in, loud and full of high energy.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating ~4.1 combined with uniformly positive comments about both performance and sound quality yields a solid 4‑star recommendation.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with well‑balanced levels; praised for CM upgrades and lack of noticeable dropouts or muffiness.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Good Times Bad Times > Not Fade Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set deemed average with some meandering, while the second set is tighter, more energetic and packed with jam highlights.

band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir's rhythm guitar/vocals described as "slashing" early in the first set; his song Here Comes Sunshine noted as well‑jammed.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum segment into The Other One is called a "face melting explosion," indicating an especially powerful performance.
